Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 2a) demonstrates marked asymmetry of the pulmonary vasculature with a diminutive right hilum and reduced vascular markings in the right lung, indicative of chronic right pulmonary artery hypoplasia or obstruction. This finding is consistent with the known vascular involvement in Takayasu arteritis and correlates with the CT evidence of vessel wall pathology, rather than an acute embolic event or bilateral disease.
